## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13008#issuecomment-5790565636) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13008#issuecomment-5791091019), checked at `c8fc9ba4`. The earlier observation is resolved. One minor new state issue is reported below.

**Verified:** A left-click on the chevron now pins the drawer through `drawerPinned`. The pin survives hover exit in both the horizontal and vertical layouts, and a second click collapses the drawer even while the pointer is still over it. Open manage or tray-item menus still keep the drawer revealed.

| Earlier claim (at `52f8fa61`) | At `c8fc9ba4` |
| --- | --- |
| Click does not pin the drawer: hover exit clears `expanded` | Resolved: hover exit only updates `drawerAreaHovered` and the suppression flag; `drawerPinned` is untouched |
| Left-click toggles `expanded` | Updated: left-click calls `toggleExpanded()`, which toggles `drawerPinned`; `expanded` is now derived and read-only |
| An open menu keeps the drawer revealed; popup close clears both menu flags | Still holds |

### Hover stays suppressed after an unpin without hover

`toggleExpanded()` sets `drawerHoverSuppressed = true` on every unpin, but the only reset is in the hover-exit branch of the two `HoverHandler`s. When the unpin arrives while `drawerAreaHovered` is false (the tap-without-hover path that the new test models), no hover exit follows, so the flag stays set.

```text
step            pinned  areaHovered  suppressed  drawer
tap (pin)       true    false        false       open
tap (unpin)     false   false        true        closed
mouse enters    false   true         true        stays closed
mouse leaves    false   false        false       closed
mouse enters    false   true         false       open
```

The trace comes from source and a simulation of statements extracted from `Tray.qml`; it was not observed on touch hardware. Both layouts behave the same. Mouse-only use is unaffected, because clicking the chevron already hovers the drawer area. The sequence does not occur at `52f8fa61`.

**Impact:** After the drawer is tapped closed, the first mouse hover does not reveal it until the pointer leaves and re-enters. Whether a real touchscreen tap leaves `drawerAreaHovered` false depends on Qt event ordering, which was not tested.

**Suggested change:** Suppress hover on unpin only when the area is currently hovered:

```qml
drawerPinned = false
drawerHoverSuppressed = drawerAreaHovered
```

Clearing the flag on every hover change is an alternative. In the extracted-statement simulation, either change fixes this sequence and leaves the other traced sequences unchanged, and `test/shell.d/tray-test.sh` still passes. Adding `sim.setHovered(true)` and an `expanded === true` assertion after the second touch tap in that test fails at `c8fc9ba4`.

**Optional test improvement:** The new behavior assertions run against `TrayStateSimulator`, a copy of the logic inside the test; `Tray.qml` itself is only checked by four source regexes. In a sandboxed run, each of these single edits to `Tray.qml` still passed all 32 assertions: removing the hover-exit suppression reset, making the left-click branch a no-op, and dropping the menu flags from `revealProgress`. Moving the drawer state transitions into a small JS helper used by both `Tray.qml` and the test (as `TrayModel.js` already is) would let the test catch such regressions.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source inspection of the new commit and the shared bar and popup components. JS evaluation of drawer-state statements extracted from `Tray.qml` (not a QML runtime). `test/shell.d/tray-test.sh` and the single-edit variants ran in an isolated sandbox under Deno's Node compatibility layer, not Node.js. No QML runtime, visual, pointer-timing, animation, popup-positioning or touch-hardware tests.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
